paper_metadata.title: Entity Linking: An Issue to Extract Corresponding Entity With Knowledge Base

evidence.excerpt: Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/ACCESS.2017.2787787

paper_metadata.abstract: Entity linking is a task to extract query mentions in documents, and then link them to their corresponding entities in a knowledge base. It can improve the performances of knowledge network construction, knowledge fusion, information retrieval, natural language processing, and knowledge base population. In this paper, we introduce the difficulties and applications of entity linking and focus on the main methods to address this issue. At last, we list the knowledge bases, data sets, and the evaluation criterion and some challenges of entity linking.

problem_addressed: The paper surveys entity linking as the problem of identifying ambiguous named-entity mentions in natural-language text and mapping them to the corresponding entities in a knowledge base, including deciding when a mention has no corresponding knowledge-base entity. It positions entity linking as a prerequisite for knowledge-base population and knowledge fusion.

methodology.description: This is a survey and framework paper rather than a single newly trained entity-linking system. Its general execution pipeline is: (1) detect query mentions with named-entity recognition or word segmentation; (2) generate candidate entities from a knowledge base using a surface-form dictionary, direct indexed search, or mention-entity probability p(e|m); (3) rank or classify candidates using context similarity, lexical/type/popularity/topic features, probabilistic or classical machine-learning models, neural semantic representations, or graph-based collective inference; (4) select the top entity when its score exceeds a threshold, otherwise output NIL; and (5) optionally cluster NIL mentions referring to the same unseen entity using string similarity, hierarchical agglomerative clustering, or semantic graphs. The paper also distinguishes coreference resolution, which clusters mentions within text, from entity linking, which maps mentions to knowledge-base entities.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: The reviewed methods rely on an external knowledge base rather than discovering an ontology or schema. Discussed resources include Wikipedia, DBpedia, YAGO, and TAC-KBP. DBpedia is described as representing entities with URIs, attributes, values, and RDF structure; Wikipedia-derived surface forms, redirects, disambiguation pages, hyperlinks, and aliases support candidate generation and disambiguation.

evaluation.setting: Survey-level comparison of entity-linking methods, knowledge bases, benchmark datasets, and evaluation criteria. The paper does not report a new controlled experiment with a single system, dataset split, or baseline configuration.

value: The paper organizes entity linking into candidate entity generation, candidate entity disambiguation, linking-result selection, and optional NIL clustering.

Candidate generation is surveyed through dictionary construction, direct knowledge-base search, and probability-based selection; disambiguation is surveyed through similarity computation, machine learning, deep learning, and graph-based methods.

The review reports that a cited deep semantic relatedness model improved accuracy by 19.4% and 24.5% on two publicly available datasets; this is a result attributed to the cited method, not a new experiment in this paper.
The paper identifies Accuracy, Precision, Recall, Fα, micro averaging, macro averaging, and separate InKB/NIL evaluation as common assessment choices.
